current.text: Experts rank him pick 1 or 2 in 9-cat drafts. The newest call is to take him at 1 or 2 in basically every format.
His best case is the number 1 finish and his downside is around 5th, so he is a safe pick at the top.
Experts value him at about 70 USD in auctions. A mock price of 80 USD was called a little high but not outrageous.
He played about 29 minutes a game last season. His usage rose to 35 over the final 13 games.
He has room to grow from that late-season usage.
His minutes are expected to be managed somewhat, with no 35 a night. The Spurs are deep and could keep minutes low after their long playoff run.
Fears about his durability are overblown. His one shortened season came from a blood clot, which is not expected to repeat.
Opponents avoid shooting at the rim against him. That cut his contests and his blocks to a career low of 3.1 last season.
One expert expects teams to keep avoiding the rim against him this regular season. Another sees his blocks landing anywhere from below 3 back up to 3.5.
Good round two partners for him include LaMelo Ball, Stephen Curry, Alperen Sengun and Anthony Davis.
The Spurs are projected as a top team in the West, with one prediction of 63 wins.
With a March 28 end, the Spurs play 3, 4 and 3 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21. They have only 13 back-to-backs.
The fantasy playoff schedule is okay but not great.

durable.text: Blocks are his biggest edge by far. Points and rebounds are also league outliers.
Turnovers are his one weak category, at about 2.8 per game.
He helps in every category except turnovers. Assists, threes and steals are his weakest positive categories.
He makes about two threes a game, which is a lot for a center.
He is one of the Spurs' best free throw shooters.
He does not win blocks on his own. You need at least one other shot blocker.
Half of his rim contests turn into blocks.
He is the best defender in the league.
He is still learning to score one-on-one. That is not yet a strength of his game.
One of his shortened seasons was caused by a blood clot.

note: He is a consensus top 2 pick in 9-cat, with elite blocks, points and rebounds, and only turnovers hurt. That makes him a natural anchor for a punt TO build, though you still need a second shot blocker. Experts value him at about 70 USD, but the market runs hotter: 77.4 USD average on Yahoo, 81.7 USD on ESPN, and 85 USD in our league last season. Above about 80 USD, the extra has to come out of the rest of your roster. Early in the season, check whether his minutes climb above last season's 29 and whether opponents keep avoiding the rim, which held his blocks to 3.1.
